candidates.change_summary: Change the function to return the negation of the stored mapping value, so approved addresses become unapproved and vice versa.
Replace the assignment that sets approvedLoggers[_logger] = _status with the inverted boolean assignment, storing ! _status instead of _status.
Remove the onlyOwner modifier from the function so any caller can change approvedLoggers.
Change the onlyOwner modifier to require msg.sender != _contractOwner instead of equality, inverting the ownership check.
Change the assignment to set the approved logger mapping at msg.sender instead of the provided _logger address.
Replace the assignment to approvedLoggers[_logger] with the opposite boolean value, causing setApprovedLogger to store ! _status instead of _status.
Remove the onlyOwner modifier from setApprovedLogger so any caller can change approvedLoggers.
Insert a require that only allows changes when _logger is not the zero address; otherwise revert preventing changes for zero address.
Change onlyOwner modifier to check msg.sender != _contractOwner (invert), so only non-owners are allowed, affecting calls that rely on onlyOwner (like setApprovedLogger).
Replace the authorization check to always allow logging by removing the approvedToLog gate and always emitting Created and returning true.
Invert the authorization check so that callers who are approved are denied (return false) and unapproved callers proceed to emit the event and return true.
Change return value when not approved: emit the event anyway but return true instead of false for unapproved callers.
Make the function always return false while still emitting the event (so callers observe a different return value).
Emit Created only for approved callers; unapproved callers return true without emitting (return value differs for some callers).
Invert the permission check so function returns true when caller is NOT an approved logger and proceeds to emit (changes return for callers that are approved vs not).
Remove the permission check so function always emits and returns true regardless of approvedLoggers (changes return for callers that are not approved).
Change return value on permission-fail from false to true so even when not approved the function returns true (but still does not emit).
Change the emitted timestamp from block.timestamp to 0, altering only the return value path by keeping emit but making no other checks.
Invert the approve check so approved callers are rejected (returns false) and unapproved callers proceed to emit and return true.
Remove the approval check entirely so every caller emits and returns true (previously some returned false), changing returned value for unapproved callers.
Change the function to return false after emitting instead of true, so callers get a different boolean despite the same emission.
